record.paper_title: Selection Principles and Special Sets of Reals
record.original_question: Is there a model of ZFC containing uncountable sets of reals with S1(Ω, Γ) such that nevertheless, for every such set X and every Hausdorff-dimension-zero set Y, the product X × Y still has Hausdorff dimension zero?

evidence.quote: Is it consistent (relative to ZFC) that there are uncountable sets of reals satisfying S1(Ω, Γ), but for each such set X and each set Y with Hausdorff dimension zero, X × Y has Hausdorff dimension zero?

artifact.self_contained_problem:
For a topological space $X$, let $\Omega$ denote the family of $\omega$-covers of $X$ (open covers $\mathcal{U}$ such that $X\notin\mathcal{U}$ and every finite subset of $X$ is contained in some member of $\mathcal{U}$), and let $\Gamma$ denote the family of $\gamma$-covers of $X$ (infinite open covers $\mathcal{U}$ such that for every $x\in X$, the set $\{U\in\mathcal{U} : x\notin U\}$ is finite). The selection principle $\mathsf{S}_1(\Omega,\Gamma)$ asserts that for every sequence $(\mathcal{U}_n)_{n\in\mathbb{N}}$ of $\omega$-covers of $X$, one can choose $U_n\in\mathcal{U}_n$ such that $\{U_n : n\in\mathbb{N}\}$ is a $\gamma$-cover of $X$. The Hausdorff dimension of a metric space is defined in the usual way via Hausdorff measures.

Question: Is it consistent with $\mathsf{ZFC}$ that there exist uncountable sets of real numbers satisfying $\mathsf{S}_1(\Omega,\Gamma)$, while simultaneously, for every such set $X\subseteq\mathbb{R}$ satisfying $\mathsf{S}_1(\Omega,\Gamma)$ and every set $Y\subseteq\mathbb{R}$ of Hausdorff dimension zero, the product $X\times Y\subseteq\mathbb{R}^2$ has Hausdorff dimension zero?
artifact.status_search_result: A targeted web search did not return any paper resolving the consistency question on the existence of uncountable $\mathsf{S}_1(\Omega,\Gamma)$ sets of reals whose products with all Hausdorff-dimension-zero sets remain of Hausdorff dimension zero. No source confirming a solution (positive or negative) was found, so the current status is unclear from publicly available evidence.
